title: Documentation
text: MarkdownUtil helps you write documentation in Markdown files, ideally in a Git repository.

title: Documentation
text: This tool is for people who write documentation in Markdown files, ideally in a Git repository. No vendor lock-in: your documentation remains a collection of ordinary Markdown files. Generate breadcrumb navigation in rendered HTML from your Markdown file structure. Generate a static HTML site from your documentation. Open-source project on GitHub .

title: Documentation
text: Setup - How to install and set up the tool Usage - How to use the tool Features - An overview of the features Other Tools - More established tools with similar goals

title: Features
text: Linter - An overview of the included linter and its rules HTML Renderer - Renders static HTML pages from Markdown files Sidebar - Describes the generated sidebar and how to control its order Breadcrumb navigation is generated from the Markdown file structure during rendering; source files remain unchanged.

title: Setup
text: MarkdownUtil is distributed as a .NET tool through NuGet . It requires .NET 10.

title: Setup
text: Install the .NET 10 runtime for your operating system.

title: Setup
text: Install the tool globally for your system or locally for a repository.

title: Setup
text: dotnet tool install --global MarkdownUtil

title: Setup
text: A local tool is available in the repository and its subfolders. A local tool requires a tool manifest. dotnet new tool-manifest # if you are setting up this repo for the first time dotnet tool install --local MarkdownUtil

title: Usage
text: Run commands from the project folder. Commands that read Markdown use ./docs or ./Docs by default. render and serve write the generated site to ./site . For a project with a Docs directory: mdu lint mdu render mdu serve mdu lint reads the Markdown files and reports any problems. mdu render writes the static site to ./site and exits. mdu serve renders the site to ./site , opens it in your browser, and watches Markdown files and linked local assets for changes. Press Ctrl+C to stop the preview server. Both render and serve generate breadcrumb navigation in the HTML from the Markdown file structure. The Markdown files are left unchanged. For example, a missing local link is reported with its file and line: /project/Docs/Overview.md:7: MDU004 LocalLinkExists: Local link target './intro.md' does not exist. Linter detected 1 error. You can specify the source directory, output directory, and port when needed. The preview defaults to ./site and port 4173 . mdu render ./Docs ./site mdu serve ./Docs ./site --port 4173 Use --no-browser to start the server without opening a browser.

title: Other Tools
text: Static site generators for Markdown documentation are not new, and many good solutions already exist. Please note: This project was created to follow the principle of "eating our own dog food" and should be understood in that context. This tool is tailored to the author's current needs and may introduce breaking changes at any time. This policy will remain in place until the project reaches an appropriate level of production readiness. Check out the other tools if you are looking for an established project with a much larger community.

title: Other Tools
text: This is a short list of interesting free alternatives from the author's perspective. It is not intended to be comprehensive. Docusaurus - Free documentation platform built with React by Meta, with source code on GitHub . MkDocs - Free Python-based documentation generator, with source code on GitHub . VuePress - Free Vue-powered static site generator, with source code on GitHub .

title: Sidebar
text: When you run mdu serve , MarkdownUtil creates a collapsible sidebar from the Markdown files in the documentation folder. A README.md represents its folder in the navigation, and child folders appear nested below it. By default, entries at the same level are sorted alphabetically by page title. Add a sidebar.order number to a page's YAML front matter to choose its position. Smaller numbers appear first. Pages with an order are listed before pages without one; unordered pages remain alphabetical. If two pages have the same order, they are sorted alphabetically by title.

title: Sidebar
text: Put the sidebar field at the top of the Markdown file, before its title. For example, this front matter in Docs/Setup/README.md places Setup before the other top-level sections: --- sidebar: order: 10 --- The MarkdownUtil documentation uses this ordering for its top-level sections: Page sidebar.order Docs/Setup/README.md 10 Docs/Usage/README.md 20 Docs/Features/README.md 30 Docs/OtherTools/README.md 40 For a single setting, you can also use the compact form: --- sidebar.order: 10 --- MarkdownUtil recognizes sidebar.order as a compact alternative to the nested form. If both sidebar: { order: ... } and sidebar.order: ... are present, the nested form takes precedence. The numbers only order siblings at the same level. For example, the value in Docs/Features/README.md positions the Features section among the other top-level sections. Values in files beneath Docs/Features/ control their positions inside that section.

title: Sidebar
text: Set sidebar.visible to false to omit a page from the sidebar. Pages are visible by default. If the page represents a folder, its child pages remain visible at the next higher level: --- sidebar: visible: false ---

title: HTML Renderer
text: Light and dark themes, with an automatic mode that follows the operating system. A collapsible, responsive sitemap navigation. Responsive, mobile-first layouts. Syntax highlighting for code blocks. Client-side search with direct links to matching sections and highlighted occurrences. Automatic copying of assets to the output directory. Breadcrumb navigation generated from the Markdown file structure.

title: HTML Renderer
text: The embedded HTML template is rendered by HtmlRenderer using .NET string and HTML-encoding APIs; it has no separate template engine dependency. Markdig renders Markdown (CommonMark) files as HTML. Search creates a static JSON index at render time; the browser searches it locally without a search service.

title: Linter
text: Rule 1 - Every Markdown page must have a level-one heading that defines its title (after any YAML front matter). Rule 2 - Directory names must match the title in the index file ( README.md ). Rule 3 - The casing of internal links in a Markdown file must match the casing of their targets. Rule 4 - Local links and image targets must point to an existing file or to a directory with a README.md index. Each diagnostic includes a stable code, a descriptive rule name, the source path, and the line number. For example, MDU004 is named LocalLinkExists : /project/Docs/Overview.md:7: MDU004 LocalLinkExists: Local link target './intro.md' does not exist. The linter also lists completely orphaned pages: pages hidden from the sidebar with sidebar.visible: false that no visible page links to. This list is informational and does not affect the lint exit code.

title: Rule 3
text: The casing of internal links must match the casing of their targets on the local file system.

title: Rule 3
text: When documentation is edited on a case-insensitive file system (such as the default file system on Windows), an incorrectly cased internal link may go unnoticed and later fail on a case-sensitive deployment.

title: Rule 3
text: For example, you might link to the parent page that contains an overview: Click [here](../README.md) to return to the overview page. If the parent file is actually named readme.md , the link may still work on a Windows machine but be broken on Linux, where file name casing matters.

title: Rule 2
text: The name of a directory containing a README.md file must match the title in that file.

title: Rule 2
text: README.md files act as index files that readers open when they enter a directory, so they typically contain the most important information about it. However, their titles may not indicate what the directory contains. When the directory name matches the README title, readers can tell what the index covers while navigating the project. For example, if a README.md file is in a docs directory, its title should be Docs .

title: Rule 2
text: Assume a README.md file with the following content: # notes These are my notes. It is good practice to name the directory notes as well.

title: Rule 2
text: Titles such as "Rule 2: This is a following description" are truncated at the colon to avoid long directory names.
